summary: This is a well‑executed, preregistered paired confirmatory study comparing a verifier‑assisted generate→validate→repair pipeline to single‑shot LLM generation (shared_initial design) for pre‑deployment NetOps changes. Execution and archival artifacts are comprehensive and consistent with the preregistration. Results show near‑ceiling baseline performance (299/300) and a single guarded rescue (300/300), producing a negligible absolute paired improvement (0.00333), wide practical null due to ceiling effects, and an exact McNemar two‑sided p=1.0. The manuscript transparently discloses methods, limitations, and artifact hashes. Overall the work is reproducible and useful as an artifact‑backed negative/limiting result about measured verifier marginality under high‑quality LLM outputs on a synthetic suite.
critical_issues: The manuscript omits a concise, human‑readable excerpt or summary of the single automated repair that produced the lone discordant (guarded‑only) rescue even though the low‑level repair trace is archived in the execution bundle; the paper currently states the repair transcript is not reproduced in the representative excerpt. Readers require a short, concrete repair example (or a one‑paragraph summary of its actions) to assess the nature of the rescue.

The paper reports an exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0 for discordant counts n10=1, n01=0 without a brief description of the exact test implementation and why the p‑value equals 1.0 in this case. This is statistically surprising to some readers and requires a short clarification referencing the exact test/executor implementation used (paired_binary_analysis_v1) and the interpretation given the extreme ceiling and minimal discordance.
required_revisions: Include a short human‑readable excerpt or concise one‑paragraph summary of the automated repair applied in the single discordant (n10=1) episode, taken from the archived repair trace. If privacy/security prohibits verbatim reproduction, provide an explicit, artifact‑traceable description of the repair (path and SHA and the minimal human‑readable summary of commands or the semantic change performed).

Add a brief methods/analysis clarification stating the exact McNemar implementation used (paired_binary_analysis_v1), the two‑sided exact test convention applied, and explain why the test yields p=1.0 for the observed discordant pattern (n10=1, n01=0). Reference the archived analysis artifact (analysis/results.json or analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) for verification.
optional_revisions: Explicitly state in Methods that the preregistered pilot (n=60) was not executed and that the main N=300 was used as pre‑specified; expand one sentence to explain whether and how this affected the original power justification (the manuscript already discloses the pilot omission, but an explicit line tying this to power limitations would improve clarity).

Condense or rephrase sections that read like provenance bookkeeping so the paper reads more like a conference scientific paper (e.g., move long artifact‑path enumerations to the artifact bundle/appendix and keep the main text focused on methods, estimand, and interpretation).

If space permits within the five‑page constraint, include a short table summarizing the repair types (semantic class) observed across runs (here only one), linking that taxonomy to the failure‑mode discussion.
